title: Planning a community event
goal: Diferenciar un plan previo de una decisión tomada en el momento.
strategy: En el diálogo, preguntate qué decisión ya estaba tomada antes de hablar. Esa distinción explica el contraste entre going to y will mejor que traducir ambas como futuro.
passage:
Sara: We’re going to organise a book exchange on Saturday. I’ve already booked the room.
Ben: Great. How are people going to find out about it?
Sara: We’re going to put posters in the library. I designed them yesterday.
Ben: I’ll share the information with my neighbours, then.
Sara: Thanks. Oh, there are only six chairs in the room.
Ben: Don’t worry. I’ll bring four more from the office.
Sara: Look at those clouds. It’s going to rain.
Ben: Then we’ll keep the books inside.
questions: Which action was planned before the conversation?
Sara ya diseñó los afiches. Las otras dos acciones se ofrecen durante la conversación.
She has visible evidence in the clouds.
“Look at those clouds” aporta evidencia presente para la predicción.
task: Escribí un diálogo para organizar una actividad. Incluí dos planes previos con going to, un ofrecimiento con will y una predicción con evidencia.
model: A: We’re going to clean the community garden on Sunday. We bought the tools yesterday. B: Great. I’ll bring some water for everyone. A: We’re going to start at nine, before it gets hot. B: Look at that broken gate. Someone is going to have trouble opening it. A: You’re right. I’ll ask the organiser to check it today.
checklist: Después de will usé la forma base.
Mi predicción con going to incluye evidencia presente.
contrast: Will es un modal: va seguido de infinitivo sin to.
